item.content:encoded: Will the shareholders of Tata Sons, the holding company of the salt-to-software conglomerate, have the final say on the company’s proposed stock exchange listing, or will the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandate on compulsory listing prevail? Domain experts are scanning the RBI Act, which was enacted in 1934 and amended several times thereafter, to find an answer to that question, which is at the centre of the biggest corporate battle of the time.

item.title: Oil, gas import bill up 60% in Oct as Brent surges, LPG use declines
item.description: Direct private LPG imports fell 83.8 per cent in October and 97.3 per cent in April-October. Packed domestic LPG sales by state-run companies fell 11.8 per cent in October, and bulk LPG sales fell ...
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60 per cent year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude averaged $124.77 a barrel, almost double that of a year earlier, according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), part of the oil ministry.The net bill was $10.0 billion in October 2025. Crude imports alone cost $19.5 billion, against $10.4 billion a year ago, even though volumes rose only 11 per cent to 23.3 million tonnes. LNG imports cost $1.3 billion, and petroleum product exports brought in $6.3 billion.Brent averaged $116.77 in September and $64.75 in October 2025. The Indian basket averaged $119.91 in October, against $65.08 a year earlier.Over April-October, the net import bill reached $97.7 billion, up from $70.3 billion a year earlier. Crude imports rose 2.7 per cent in volume but cost $111.0 billion, against $72.3 billion.Consumption of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fell 12.3 per cent in October and 15.1 per cent in April-October. The number of active domestic LPG customers stood at 32.6 crore on November 1, down from 33.4 crore on April 1, the PPAC data showed.Direct private LPG imports fell 83.8 per cent in October and 97.3 per cent in April-October. Packed domestic LPG sales by state-run companies fell 11.8 per cent in October, and bulk LPG sales fell 49.1 per cent. Auto LPG sales rose 23.9 per cent.Imports of petroleum products fell 41.2 per cent in October and 49.3 per cent in the fiscal year so far. PPAC attributed the fiscal-year decline mainly to lower imports of LPG, pet coke and fuel oil.The International Energy Agency said in its World Energy Outlook 2026 that LPG imports fell by over 50 per cent in the first two months of shipping disruption through the Strait of Hormuz.Other fuels held up better. Diesel consumption rose 12 per cent in October to 8.5 million tonnes, petrol rose 3.5 per cent, and bitumen rose 16.5 per cent. Total petroleum product consumption rose 2.7 per cent to 20.5 million tonnes in October. It was still down 3.2 per cent in April-October at 134.2 million tonnes.Natural gas consumption fell 7.27 per cent to 5,707 million standard cubic metres in October. LNG imports fell 6.94 per cent to 3,014 million standard cubic metres.India processed 24.1 million tonnes of crude in October, up 7.1 per cent, or about 5.70 million barrels a day. Of that, 22.0 million tonnes were imported crude, and domestic output was 2.1 million tonnes. Imports met 88.7 per cent of crude consumption in October.Domestic crude and condensate output was 2.3 million tonnes. Import dependency for natural gas stood at 52.8 per cent in October.Ethanol blending in petrol stood at 20 per cent in October, PPAC data showed.

item.title: Weddings, festivals, price hikes to brighten Q3 outlook for paint companies
item.description: Paint companies expect stronger demand and volume growth in Q3FY27, but margins remain under pressure as price increases have yet to fully offset input cost inflation ...
item.dc:creator: Ram Prasad Sahu
item.content:encoded: After a steady show in the September quarter (Q2FY27), the outlook for the paints sector is expected to be strong. Strong demand, healthy offtake and price hikes could lead to an improvement in volume and revenue growth in Q3. In addition to the shift in the festive calendar to the December (Q3FY27) quarter, moderation of the competitive intensity in the sector and easing of margin concerns given the correction in crude oil prices are the other triggers for the sector.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / News / Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research

Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research The announcement was made during the institute's platinum jubilee celebrations on November 21

The funding will primarily support applied AI research in areas such as Indic languages, agriculture, materials science and educational technology (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India Kolkata 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 22 2026 | 1:39 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Google has pledged $5 million to IIT Kharagpur to strengthen advanced artificial intelligence (AI) research, expand educational opportunities and develop the next generation of technology professionals, a senior institute official said on Sunday. The announcement was made during the institute's platinum jubilee celebrations on November 21. IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty told PTI that Sundar Pichai, an alumnus and CEO of Google, played a key role in facilitating the funding for IIT Kharagpur. " We are proud of him (Sundar Pichai) as an alumnus who heads Google. We are thankful to Google for pledging the money, and Pichai assisted in IIT Kharagpur getting the money," he said.   The funding will primarily support applied AI research in areas such as Indic languages, agriculture, materials science and educational technology. Also Read

The grant will be channelled through three broad areas -- advanced AI research, educational opportunities, including expansion of AI training and curriculum for students and faculty, and capacity building through the development of campus AI infrastructure, frameworks and tools. The director said another alumnus, Jyoti Chatterjee, had pledged an additional $5 million as seed endowment for developing a next-generation data initiative. "The contributions are expected to provide a major boost to the institute's efforts to expand AI-driven innovation and enhance its role in developing skilled technology professionals," he said.
